topic: Theme C: The Existence of God & Revelation
subject: religious-studies

items.title: Muslims believe the Quran is the direct, unchanged word of God
items.claim: How do Muslims understand the origin of the Quran?

options.text: A collection of Muhammad's wise sayings, gathered over centuries
Revealed directly by God to Muhammad through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) over 23 years (610-632 CE), to be recited and transmitted unchanged in Arabic
A revised version of the Bible adapted for Arabia
A book written by Muhammad based on his teachings

items.reveal:
The word 'Quran' comes from the Arabic root q-r-' meaning 'to recite'. The first revelation (Sura 96, 'Iqra' — Recite!) at Mount Hira around 610 CE.

The Quran was compiled in written form under Caliph Uthman (around 650 CE), with non-conforming versions destroyed to ensure a single authoritative text. Muslims regard the Arabic text — not translations — as the Quran proper.

The Hadith (sayings of Muhammad) is a distinct category, recorded by his companions, with major Sunni collections by Bukhari (d. 870) and Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj (d. 875).
items.why: The Quran's status differs sharply from how Christians treat the Bible (composed by human authors under divine inspiration). Islamic theology treats every Arabic word as direct divine speech — which is why translation is always a 'meaning of' the Quran.

items.title: Muslims believe the Quran was revealed via the angel Gabriel
items.claim: How do Muslims understand the Quran's origin?

options.text: Muhammad's wise sayings, gathered over centuries
The direct word of God, revealed to Muhammad through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) over 23 years (610-632 CE), to be recited and transmitted unchanged in Arabic
A revised version of the Bible adapted for Arabia

items.reveal:
The word 'Quran' comes from the Arabic root q-r-' meaning 'to recite'. The first revelation (Sura 96, 'Iqra' — 'Recite!') is dated to around 610 CE at the Cave of Hira on Mount Jabal al-Nour.

The Quran was compiled in written form under the third caliph Uthman (around 650 CE), with non-conforming versions destroyed to ensure a single authoritative text. Muslims regard only the Arabic text as the Quran proper; translations are 'meanings of' the Quran.

The Hadith — sayings of Muhammad — is a separate category, compiled by his companions and successors. Major Sunni collections: Sahih al-Bukhari (d. 870) and Sahih Muslim (d. 875).
items.why: The Quran's status differs from how Christians understand the Bible. Islamic theology treats every Arabic word as direct divine speech — which is why translation is always 'the meaning of' rather than 'the Quran'.

items.title: Jihad has greater and lesser meanings in classical Islam
items.claim: What is the greater/lesser jihad distinction?

options.text: Both refer only to armed warfare

A widely cited hadith distinguishes lesser jihad (armed struggle in defence of the community) from greater jihad (inner struggle against one's own ego); the hadith's authenticity is debated but the inner-struggle understanding is found in independent Sufi and mainstream piety traditions
Jihad refers only to economic struggle

items.reveal:
The Arabic root j-h-d means 'to strive, to exert effort'. The greater/lesser distinction is attributed to a hadith reported by al-Bayhaqi and al-Khatib al-Baghdadi: 'We have returned from the lesser jihad to the greater jihad — the jihad against the self.'

Ibn Taymiyya (d. 1328) and some modern scholars question the hadith's chain of authentication. But the inner-struggle theme appears widely in Sufi writing and is not dependent on the hadith alone.

Classical Islamic law (fiqh) regulates armed jihad with conditions on declaration, conduct, and protection of non-combatants — distinct from later extremist appropriations of the term.
items.why: A word picked up by 21st-century media can carry meanings that don't match its theological tradition. 'Jihad' in classical Islam is far more various than its English-language press usage.
